details:
LunaSite is a Lunar Landing Site Suitability and Navigation System developed to support the exploration and preliminary assessment of potential lunar landing locations.

Selecting a suitable lunar landing site is a challenging task because the lunar surface contains craters, uneven terrain, elevation variations, steep slopes and changing illumination conditions. Understanding these factors is important for future lunar exploration, lander operations and surface mobility.

Our project provides an interactive 3D lunar environment where users can explore the Moon, visualize different lunar data layers and examine potential landing regions. It integrates lunar surface imagery, elevation and slope information to help users understand the characteristics of selected locations.

The system includes an interactive 3D Moon visualization using CesiumJS, NASA lunar imagery and terrain layers, a time-based lunar lighting visualization component, and a preliminary landing-site assessment module. The terrain assessment processes elevation and slope data to calculate parameters such as mean slope, maximum slope and surface roughness. These parameters are combined into a preliminary suitability score to support comparative analysis.

We use NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter datasets, including Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Wide Angle Camera (LROC WAC) imagery and Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA) elevation and slope data.

Technology stack:
Frontend: HTML, CSS, JavaScript and CesiumJS.
Backend: Python and FastAPI.
Scientific and geospatial processing: NumPy, Rasterio, PyProj and Skyfield.

The project was developed through research, data processing, visualization and AI-assisted development workflows. We aim to make lunar terrain information easier to explore and interpret through one integrated platform.

LunaSite is a preliminary decision-support prototype, not a certified lunar landing safety system. Its current assessment methodology has limitations and requires further scientific validation and additional hazard analysis before operational use.
